title: A Complaint about a Delivery
description: Four recordings about a late parcel: a complaint call, a driver's message, a staff discussion and a recorded company message.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer (A, B or C) for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · The complaint call
parts.intro: You will hear Mr Cooper phoning the customer service of a delivery company. The agent is called Emma.

script.speaker: Emma
script.text: Good afternoon, Swift Parcels customer service, Emma speaking. How can I help you?

script.speaker: Mr Cooper
script.text: Hello. I'm calling about an order that was supposed to arrive last Tuesday. It's now Monday, and I still haven't received it.

script.speaker: Emma
script.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Could you tell me what you ordered?

script.speaker: Mr Cooper
script.text: A pair of walking boots for my son's school trip. The trip is on Friday, so now I'm worried.

script.speaker: Emma
script.text: I understand. Let me check. Our system says the parcel was delivered on Wednesday to number twelve, Park Road.

script.speaker: Mr Cooper
script.text: That's wrong. I live at number twenty-one, not twelve. Someone has mixed up the numbers.

script.speaker: Emma
script.text: I see. That's our driver's mistake, and I apologise. Could you ask the neighbours at number twelve if they have it?

script.speaker: Mr Cooper
script.text: I did that this morning. Nobody was in, but I left a note.

script.speaker: Emma
script.text: Thank you. If the parcel doesn't turn up by tomorrow, I'll send you a new pair with express delivery, at no extra cost. You'd get them on Thursday.

script.speaker: Mr Cooper
script.text: That would be a relief. Thank you for your help.

parts.title: Part 2 · The driver's message
parts.intro: You will hear a voicemail message from a delivery driver, Raj.

script.speaker: Raj
script.text: Hello, this is Raj, a driver with Swift Parcels. I'm calling about the boots you ordered. First, I want to say sorry. I've just spoken to my manager, and I know I made a mistake.

script.speaker: Raj
script.text: On Wednesday morning, I was in a hurry, because my van had a flat tyre and I was running late. I read the address too quickly and left your box at number twelve.

script.speaker: Raj
script.text: This afternoon, I went back to Park Road and knocked at number twelve. A young woman answered, and she'd found your note. She says she wasn't at home on Wednesday, and the parcel was left in the garden shed by her brother.

script.speaker: Raj
script.text: Good news: I've collected it, and it's in my van now. I'll bring it to your house tomorrow morning before ten o'clock. You don't need to be at home, because I can leave it with your neighbour at number twenty-three, if you agree.

script.speaker: Raj
script.text: Please call me back on this number if that's not suitable. I know you needed the boots for a school trip, so I'm very sorry for the trouble.

script.speaker: Raj
script.text: Have a good evening, and once again, apologies.

parts.title: Part 3 · Two members of staff
parts.intro: You will hear Emma talking to her team leader, Paul, about the complaint.

script.speaker: Paul
script.text: Emma, I saw your note about the Cooper complaint. How did the call go?

script.speaker: Emma
script.text: Well, he was polite, although he was worried about the school trip. The driver delivered to the wrong house.

script.speaker: Paul
script.text: That's the third mistake like that this month. We need to do something.

script.speaker: Emma
script.text: I agree. Part of the problem is that drivers have to deliver about a hundred and twenty parcels a day. They don't have time to check.

script.speaker: Paul
script.text: True, but that's no excuse. Could we ask them to take a photo of each door?

script.speaker: Emma
script.text: That could help, although some drivers might complain it takes too long. Why don't we try it with a small group first?

script.speaker: Paul
script.text: Good idea. I'll speak to the regional manager on Wednesday.

script.speaker: Emma
script.text: Also, should we offer Mr Cooper a gift? A voucher, perhaps?

script.speaker: Paul
script.text: Yes. Ten pounds off his next order. He was very patient, after all.

script.speaker: Emma
script.text: I'll write to him this afternoon.

script.speaker: Paul
script.text: Thanks. And please remind the team: apologise first, solve the problem second.

parts.title: Part 4 · A recorded message
parts.intro: You will hear the recorded message of the delivery company.

script.speaker: Operator
script.text: Thank you for calling Swift Parcels. Please listen carefully, as our menu options have changed.

script.speaker: Operator
script.text: If you want to track a parcel, press one. If you want to report a late or missing parcel, press two. For all other questions, press three.

script.speaker: Operator
script.text: Please note that parcels are normally delivered within three working days. Express orders arrive in one working day. Weekends are not counted as working days.

script.speaker: Operator
script.text: If your parcel hasn't arrived after five working days, you can claim a refund. You must complete the form on our website, and we'll reply within forty-eight hours.

script.speaker: Operator
script.text: For damaged items, please take a photograph before opening the box fully, and keep all the packaging. We cannot accept claims without photographs.

script.speaker: Operator
script.text: Our telephone lines are open from eight in the morning until eight in the evening on weekdays, and from nine until one on Saturdays. We are closed on Sundays.

script.speaker: Operator
script.text: To speak to an adviser, please stay on the line. Your call may be recorded for training purposes.
